standing: DRAFT - NOT RULED, NOT APPROVED. Drafted for Christian's review (his reply filed 29 October 2026, item 1). Nothing here is in the engine's knowledge: where this file is stored in the repository, it is a document only (docs/audits/drafts/ta02-composition/), and the engine loads none of it. Nothing here may be applied, alone or in part, before the decisions it names are his: MEASURED below, the two existence items alone refuse every GF2 game, and any out-of-play value at the game-form level changes A01 (engine limitation E-K4). Basis OWNER_RULING on an item names the ruling it rests on, and each item's rulingStatus says whether that ruling is given. Every item here rests on his standing principle (his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 10), which is given; applying it to GF2 is ours. The adaptations no ruling of his covers (where a goal kick or a kick-off is taken in this game) are proposals with rulingStatus NOT_GIVEN, never items. Loaded without E1, every OWNER_RULING item would show as APPROVED whatever its rulingStatus (rendering/review-evidence.ts:389-398).

K4-1 is a confirmation only (GF2's sentence adds nothing to Law 9). K4-D4 presents Law 8 adapted (the conceding team kicks off from the centre of the area) as the default, for confirmation or a departure.

His 26 October offside sentence is quoted in full, including "but we should not expand the current work into a comprehensive reconstruction of soccer's laws", beside the E4 strictness, the profile-data correction and the adaptations not proposed.

about: A minimal restatement that would make the possession game form's out-of-play restarts act, under the normal Laws as his 26 October principle inherits them (Law 9 for existence, Law 15 at the touchlines, Laws 16 and 17 at the end lines), with GF2's library restart sentence as agreeing text. GF2-16.a (T2 NOT_LAST_TOUCH) and GF2-16.b (T6 STOP_RESUME) address transitions keyed on OUT_END_LINE and OUT_TOUCHLINE, but no item of GF2 (or of any contract a plain GF2 composition selects) establishes such a transition: GF2's only T1 item is GF2-07.a (POSSESSION_CHANGE), and its T1 declaration for the other triggers is UNDECLARED ("Existence of other transitions never examined (START, SCORE and out-of-play exist by construction, RC-19)"), a convention SD-44 superseded. Shape: corpus-restatements.json `added[]` entries ({contractId, after, ruling, item, why}), each item in the shape of the GF2 items as loaded. `standing` and `rulingStatus` on each item are draft annotation keys (not engine keys, types.ts ENGINE_ITEM_KEYS). Ids GF2-16.c onward continue the GF2-16 family.

gf2SetupGuidance.quote: Restart conditions: ball out of play restarts from the team that didn't touch it last.

whatItDecides: If adopted: that the ball can go out of play and that play then restarts: the transitions exist (T1) and stop play (T6 STOP_RESUME, GF2-16.b).
If adopted: who restarts: the team that did not touch the ball last (T2 NOT_LAST_TOUCH, GF2-16.a).

Nothing beyond the Laws. Law 9 already makes both out-of-play transitions exist and stop play, and Laws 15, 16 and 17 already give every such restart to the team that did not touch the ball last, at the touchlines and at either goal line, under his 26 October principle (16.c-16.i). Adopting the sentence is therefore a confirmation only (K4-1).
whatItDoesNotDecide: Which player of that team takes it (T3). "restarts from the team" implies one of its players; GF2 declares T3 for out of play UNDECLARED ("Who takes an out-of-play restart was never examined."). Under his 26 October principle the Laws supply it: Law 15 at the touchline (16.e), Laws 16 and 17 at either end line (16.i).

From where (T4): GF2 declares T4 for out of play NON_CLAIMED ("doesNotConstrain: restart location."). The Laws supply it at the touchline (Law 15, 16.f). At an end line Laws 16 and 17 place the restart in the corner area or the goal area; the goal area does not exist in GF2, so that location is adapted (K4-D3).

How (T5): GF2 declares T5 for out of play NON_CLAIMED ("doesNotConstrain: whether restarts are timed or contested, read as the method"). The Laws supply it at the touchline (Law 15, a throw-in, 16.g). At an end line Laws 16 and 17 make it a kick of a stationary ball (K4-D3).

That the rule is the same at every boundary. "ball out of play" names no line; Laws 16 and 17 do: the end-line award is the same at either goal line, so T1b EACH_TEAM is the Laws' (16.h), not a reading of GF2's silence. (The uncorrected draft offered it as a reading for his confirmation.)

What happens after a score: GF2 declares T2-T6 for trigger=SCORE NOT_AUTHORED ("notAuthored: restart after a score."). Law 8 gives the kick-off, by the team that conceded, from a centre mark this game does not have (K4-D4).
Whether a restart begins a new attack (T7): GF2 declares T7 UNDECLARED. Under the RPC-003 draft this is open and tied to D1 (rpc-003-contract.DRAFT.json, ledger L-13).

adoptionQuestion.now: A confirmation only (README Q5a). Law 9 already makes both out-of-play transitions exist under his 26 October principle, and Laws 15, 16 and 17 already give GF2-16.a/b's values (the team that did not touch the ball last; play stops and restarts), so the sentence adds nothing the Laws do not. He may confirm it as GF2 knowledge, or we stop citing it as a basis; no item depends on the answer.

words: The normal Laws of the Game should apply by default wherever they are applicable, unless an activity introduces an explicit, knowledge-authorized modification.
We should not need to redefine ordinary soccer rules separately for every Learning Goal, game form, or activity.

Where a normal law cannot apply directly because of the modified field, scoring structure, or game format, the system should identify the relevant adaptation rather than silently assume conventional conditions exist.
The offside question, for example, may need an explicit ruling for this small-sided environment, but we should not expand the current work into a comprehensive reconstruction of soccer's laws.
The governing principle is to inherit established sport rules and explicitly define only the necessary departures.

whatTheLawsSupplyAtTheEndLine.award: Whenever the whole ball passes over a goal line without a score: a goal kick if a player of the attacking team touched it last, a corner kick if a player of the defending team did. Either way the restart goes to the team that did not touch the ball last (agrees with GF2-16.a, NOT_LAST_TOUCH).
whatTheLawsSupplyAtTheEndLine.sameAtEitherLine: The award is the same at either goal line, so T1b EACH_TEAM is the Laws' (16.h), not a reading of GF2's silence.
whatTheLawsSupplyAtTheEndLine.taker: A player of the team awarded the restart: the defending team takes a goal kick, the attacking team a corner kick (16.i). In GF2 each team defends the end line behind the end it is assigned (each team attacks the target opposite its own assigned end, GF2-08.c-f), so which kick applies is decidable.
whatTheLawsSupplyAtTheEndLine.needsNoGoal: Neither award depends on a goal standing at that end. Only the goal kick's location, the goal area of Law 1, does not exist in GF2. That location, and how the method is said, are what K4-D3 asks him to confirm.
whatTheLawsLeaveToAdapt: where the goal kick is taken (the goal area does not exist): proposed in K4-D3
the corner kick's corner area (the corner arc is not marked; the corner of the playing area is): proposed in K4-D3
the opponents' distances (outside the penalty area at a goal kick; 9.15 m at a corner kick), which presuppose markings and dimensions this game does not have: not proposed (K4-D3)

It is our encoding's blind spot, not the Laws.

proposedAdaptation.rulingStatus: NOT_GIVEN (our identification of the adaptation his 26 October principle asks for; for his confirmation or a departure)
proposedAdaptation.principle: Where a normal law cannot apply directly because of the modified field, scoring structure, or game format, the system should identify the relevant adaptation rather than silently assume conventional conditions exist.
proposedAdaptation.cornerKick: When a player of the team defending that end line touched the ball last: a corner kick to the other team, the ball stationary, from the corner of the playing area nearer to where the ball went out (Law 17 places the ball in the corner area nearest that point; the corner arc is not marked, the corner of the area is).
proposedAdaptation.goalKick: When a player of the team attacking that end line touched the ball last: a goal kick to the team defending it, the ball stationary, from the middle of its own end line, where a goal and its goal area would stand. The location is OUR PROPOSAL: Law 16's goal area does not exist in GF2.
proposedAdaptation.notProposed: The opponents' distances at these restarts (outside the penalty area at a goal kick; 9.15 m at a corner kick) also presuppose markings and dimensions this game does not have. We have not proposed adaptations for them, within his limit: "The offside question, for example, may need an explicit ruling for this small-sided environment, but we should not expand the current work into a comprehensive reconstruction of soccer's laws." (his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 10, christian-2026-10-26.txt:178).

conditionalOnDecision.question: How play starts, and what happens after a score. GF2 says nothing (T2-T6 for SCORE are NOT_AUTHORED in GF2's declarations, "notAuthored: restart after a score."). Law 8 decides both: a kick-off to start play and, after a goal, a kick-off by the team that conceded, from the centre mark. Only the centre mark is missing. His principle asks us to identify the adaptation: we propose it below (proposedAdaptation) and ask him only to confirm it or name a departure. Today the composed game says "Pick which team starts with the ball and tell both teams before you start" and nothing after a score.

defaultLawsMachinery.whatItIs: The Sport Profile names the Laws as the default in a declaration block (sport-profile-soccer.json defaultLaws: 10 laws, each with applicableWhen / requires predicates, listedFor ADAPTATION or DEPARTURE, and a restart flag), never as items: corpus.ts loadSportDefaultLaws, "his item 10 excludes reconstructing the laws as representation". realization/default-laws-check.ts blockLawAccountOf reads each law against a realized game as APPLIES / DEPARTED / NOT_APPLICABLE / ADAPTATION_OWED.
defaultLawsMachinery.whatItCanSupply: A STATUS per law, for an administrator (REPORT) or as a refusal (ENFORCE), and the DRAFT "normal rules apply" sentence where nothing is owed. MEASURED for plain GF2: LAW-8 and LAW-11 owed; LAW-8-DB, LAW-13, LAW-15 apply; LAW-12-GK, LAW-14, LAW-16, LAW-17, LAW-4-GK not applicable (LAW-16/17 only through our encoding's blind spot: see blindSpot).
defaultLawsMachinery.whatItCannotSupply: A value for T3, T4 or T5. The block holds no taker, location or method, and the account reads the game after derivation, so no law can close a transition line. The values must come from items. Their authority is his 26 October principle with the Laws: Law 15 at the touchline (16.e-16.g), Laws 16 and 17 at the end line (16.h, 16.i). Where a law's location presupposes a marking the game lacks (the goal area at an end line, the centre mark for a kick-off), the adaptation is ours to identify and his to confirm (K4-D3, K4-D4).
defaultLawsMachinery.withoutARealization: defaultLawsAccountOf returns null unless the realization declares defaultLawsCheck (realization/default-laws-check.ts:472, `if (!realization?.defaultLawsCheck || !input.laws) return null`), and the build reads the check only from the realization being tried (rendering/build-activity.ts lawAccountOf and gameLaws). A composed game has no realization, so it has no account, no departure check and no "normal rules apply" sentence. E4 (SYNTHESIS section 3) is the general fix: read the check from knowledge - a Sport-Profile default mode, or a context-contract field - with the strictness (REPORT or ENFORCE) his decision (README Q5). Under ENFORCE a plain GF2 composition would refuse until K4-D4 (LAW-8) and K4-D5 (LAW-11) are decided; under REPORT it would be served and the two owed adaptations listed for the administrator. His limit bears on how far E4 goes: "The offside question, for example, may need an explicit ruling for this small-sided environment, but we should not expand the current work into a comprehensive reconstruction of soccer's laws." (his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 10, christian-2026-10-26.txt:178).
defaultLawsMachinery.blindSpot: LAW-16 and LAW-17 are PER_END with applicableWhen OBJECT_OF_KIND_AT_END goal, so the account reads them as NOT_APPLICABLE wherever no goal stands and reports nothing owed at a GF2 end line. That predicate is our DRAFT encoding, written for the build-out activities (the profile's note: "Only the laws that can fail to apply in a modified environment and matter for the two build-out realizations are listed" and "The law ids, the names and the 'penalty-area' token are ours (DRAFT)", sport-profile-soccer.json:33), not the Laws: Laws 16 and 17 award the end-line restart without a goal, and only the goal kick's location (the goal area) needs adapting. Correcting the predicate, so the account reports the goal kick's location as owed an adaptation where no goal stands, is a correction to our DRAFT data, not a new law and not engine code. It should stay within his limit: "The offside question, for example, may need an explicit ruling for this small-sided environment, but we should not expand the current work into a comprehensive reconstruction of soccer's laws." (his reply filed 26 October 2026, item 10, christian-2026-10-26.txt:178).
